text:
This analysis evaluates morphological variations among Antarctic penguin species observed at the Palmer Station.
The dataset used in this analysis is from the R package palmerpenguins, created by Allison Horst, Alison Hill, and Kristen Gorman. Learn more on the palmerpenguins official site.

title: R Post
text:
1. Data Cleaning and Preparation
We load the palmerpenguins package alongside tidyverse to filter out missing records and inspect key variables.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Clean dataset removing NA values in body metrics
penguins_clean <- penguins %>%
  drop_na(species, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, sex) %>%
  mutate(
    species = as.character(species),
    bill_ratio = bill_length_mm / bill_depth_mm
  )

glimpse(penguins_clean)

#| label: r-summary-table
bill_summary <- penguins_clean %>%
  group_by(species, island) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bill_len = mean(bill_length_mm),
    mean_bill_dep = mean(bill_depth_mm),
    mean_bill_ratio = mean(bill_ratio),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_bill_ratio))

#| label: fig-r-bill-dimensions
#| fig-cap: "Bill Length vs. Bill Depth across Palmer Penguin Species."
#| fig-width: 8

ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species, shape = sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Bill Morphological Dimensions by Species",
    subtitle = "Exhibiting Simpson's Paradox across overall vs. species-level trends",
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
    color = "Species",
    shape = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )








Summary of Results Simpson’s Paradox in Action: If we looked at the dataset as a whole without grouping by species, bill depth and length would appear uncorrelated or negatively correlated. However, within each individual species, there is a clear positive correlation between bill length and bill depth.
Species Cluster Distinctiveness:
Adélie: Short bill length, high bill depth.
Chinstrap: Long bill length, high bill depth.
Gentoo: Long bill length, low bill depth.

title: About
text: I grew up with a background in engineering and geographic information science, completing my Bachelor of Engineering in Surveying and Mapping Engineering at Tongji University followed by a Master of Science in GIS at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Before starting the Master of Data Science (MDS) program at UBC, I worked as a GIS Developer at Mississippi State University’s Geosystems Research Institute. title: About
text:
Why Data Science
Throughout my work with spatial systems, I found that the most compelling challenges always came down to data: extracting signal from massive spatial datasets, building robust statistical models, and automating complex analytical pipelines. While GIS gave me a strong foundation in spatial analysis and visualization, I joined the MDS program at UBC to formalize and expand my toolkit in machine learning, high-performance computing, and structured data engineering. My goal is to bridge complex data science methodologies with real-world spatial and environmental problem-solving.

title: About

Outside of Data Science
Outside of coursework and coding, I enjoy photography, exploring local food spots, and traveling—with recent trips taking me through New Zealand, Japan, and California. On weekends, you’ll usually find me trying out new restaurants around Richmond and Vancouver, editing photos, or catching up on road trips and outdoor exploring.

title: Python Post
text:
In this analysis, we explore the physical characteristics of penguin species observed in the Palmer Archipelago, Antarctica.
The dataset used in this post is the palmerpenguins dataset, collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station, Antarctica LTER. The original source is on the official palmerpenguins documentation page.

title: Python Post
text:
In this analysis, we explore the physical characteristics of penguin species observed in the Palmer Archipelago, Antarctica.
The dataset used in this post is the palmerpenguins dataset, collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station, Antarctica LTER. The original source is on the official palmerpenguins documentation page.

title: Python Post
text:
1. Data Loading & Cleaning
First, load the dataset using palmerpenguins and clean it by removing rows with missing physical measurements.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

# Load raw penguins dataset
df_raw = load_penguins()

# Clean missing values across key physical traits
features = ['species', 'island', 'bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm', 'flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g', 'sex']
penguins = df_raw.dropna(subset=features).copy()

print(f"Loaded {len(penguins)} complete penguin observations.")
penguins.head()

#| label: summary-stats
# Group by species and compute summary statistics
species_stats = (
    penguins.groupby('species')
    .agg(
        count=('species', 'count'),
        mean_mass_g=('body_mass_g', 'mean'),
        std_mass_g=('body_mass_g', 'std'),
        mean_flipper_mm=('flipper_length_mm', 'mean'),
        mean_bill_len_mm=('bill_length_mm', 'mean')
    )
    .round(2)
    .reset_index()
)

species_stats

#| label: fig-flipper-vs-mass
#| fig-cap: "Flipper Length vs. Body Mass across Palmer Penguin Species."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=penguins,
    x="flipper_length_mm",
    y="body_mass_g",
    hue="species",
    style="sex",
    s=70,
    alpha=0.8,
    palette="Set2"
)

plt.title("Penguin Flipper Length vs. Body Mass", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
plt.xlabel("Flipper Length (mm)", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)", fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title="Species & Sex", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Loaded 333 complete penguin observations.









Summary of Results Strong Linear Relationship: There is a clear positive correlation between flipper length and body mass across all species.
Cluster Separation: Gentoo penguins form a distinct cluster in the upper-right corner (longer flippers, larger body mass), whereas Adelie and Chinstrap penguins overlap considerably in body mass but show separation along bill length and flipper length dimensions.
Sexual Dimorphism: Within every species, male penguins systematically exhibit higher body mass and longer flipper lengths than females.
